city-digital-twin · Newcastle study · project report

The twin is held back by its routing and its demand, not its constants

2026-09-25HEAD 35b6442branch praneetdhoolia/f36-read-and-gold-standardgate PASS (two checks were red at session open - the dead arm - and were fixed in 35b64421)

The twin is well instrumented and honestly documented, and it is still 2 of 12 modes inside 10 %: car and motorbike, on the newest result (F35) and on F36's first reading at iteration 230 (not a result - the arm was killed at 237 by a Windows Update restart). This pass found why the scoreboard has not moved: three defects sit UNDER the demand and the router, not in the constants the last eleven days tuned. (1) The external boundary tier - 6,103 agents, 12,206 weekday trips - is missing from the F36 plans, lost in the 16 September refactor. (2) The pt access ceiling is misderived at 1,200 m, which doubled the share of pt requests that find no transit route from 31-37 % to 66-68 % the day access moved onto the network (12 September), so 74 % of pt requests come back as a walk averaging 8.4 km - walk runs 6.5x its observed length and pt trips come out too short. (3) The taxi fleet's 16-minute wait is computed and never experienced.

Code quality rates 2-3 in most cells, 4 in six: correctness is capped by these defects, maintainability by god functions and a mechanical staging refactor, testability by untested modules on the result path. The reports have been followed (77 % of 225 recommendations taken), but the taken ones were instruments; the goal count moved once, on 14 September. The next family should open on the three fixes, priced on this build at ~25.6 h (not the 62.9 h the pricer now quotes), behind a host that cannot restart under it.

Method

Six agents, one per phase, read HEAD 35b64421 from the three collectors' output: a code reviewer (all six areas, depth declared per area), a performance analyst, a historian (all 92 PRs), a document and process reviewer, a field researcher (23 of 25 calls) and a factor researcher (8 of 15 calls). The rating rubric: five dimensions per area, 1-5, each cell with its two strongest pieces of evidence; a defect in an area caps its correctness at 3 and a defect on the result path at 2; 4 means zero defects with every risk guarded, at most a handful of long functions and no duplicated helper, no measured waste on the critical path, every result-path module unit-tested, every hard constraint held; 5 needs all of that and nothing open. Ratings are never averaged across areas. The writer measured four things itself: the no-route share of every 25 % run on disk from its own log (31-37 % before 12 September, 66-68 % after), an offline re-route of 3,000 of F36's pt trips (diagnose_pt_routing.py: 38.8-39.4 % without the cap), the plans' persons by tier against the chains (0 of 6,103 external), and the taxi fleet's logged wait.

Narrative

10 Aug: data, network and demand land in one day (#1-#3); the next morning the first MATSim run finds the 30 run-input sets do not load (#4). 11-18 Aug: the registry, zero hardcoding, the city move and the #32 network rebuild (#38); ride pairing built and found starved (#40, #43). 20-25 Aug: every mode made physical, SUMO descoped, the all-modes family F6 activated (#46-#81); the first gate fires 25 Aug. 26-31 Aug: fourteen families in six days (F7-F21) chase ride; twelve individual targets (#95); GOAL.md and the one-page board (#101); fares priced (#105). 1-8 Sep: results store, issue gate, report #1 and six more reports in six days; car first inside at a gate (F28, 7 Sep); the objective becomes the goal's maximum (#166). 9 Sep: the first result since F4 reads 0 of 12. 12 Sep: the footpath rebuild (F34) and engine routing (F35). 14 Sep: F35 arm 0 lands as the second result, 2 of 12 - still the high-water mark. Documents split; lane and recommendation ledgers. 15-17 Sep: the routers and scoring pairs, the first recommended model controls ever run, both read as nulls. 19-22 Sep: Mumbai lands on the framework; the Java fold; the roots rebuild opens F36 (#254). 23-24 Sep: F36 arm 0 runs to iteration 237 of 250 and is killed by a Windows Update reboot; read at it.230 it is 2 of 12 and not a result.

Three questions

most_important_defect
src/build/build_matsim_plans.py:1246 - the 16 September staging refactor made write_person return early for any tier-external agent (none is in B1), so the 22 September roots rebuild wrote plans with 0 of the 6,103 external boundary agents (12,206 weekday legs; plans persons 616,040 = core 510,383 + through 16,264 + freight 89,393 exactly). The whole F36 family, including the arm-0 reading at it.230, ran on a demand without its external tier; nothing in the gate or check_package compares plans persons with the chains report.
biggest_simplification
Undo the mechanical SimpleNamespace staging (34 functions in build_matsim_plans, build_activity_chains, build_matsim_run_inputs, calibrate, report_mode_ridership) into value-returning functions over small dataclass contexts, then retire src/setup/extract_loop_body.py and split_stages.py. The staging met the 150-line metric without adding cohesion, gave every function a false docstring, and carried two regressions through "byte-identical" commits (the external-agent drop and calibrate's unbound best_tag).
what_blocks_4_everywhere
Correctness: result- or record-path defects in four areas (external agents dropped; taxi wait unapplied; raw --set recorded-not-executed; stored readings from the current registry and a crashing search write-out). Testability: the demand builders and the Java engines on the result path have no unit test or probe. Maintainability: two Java god methods over 500 lines and the namespace staging. Constraint compliance: check_hardcoding's min/max blind spot lets build_population keep two modelling literals, and the manifest check ignores 579 blank retrieval dates.

architecture
A chain of standalone scripts, each a __main__ with argparse, reading the registry through registry.load() and paths through city.path(): build_population (B1) -> build_activity_chains (B2 tours + four binder passes) -> build_matsim_plans (population_v6 per day type, seed plans, bound-trip attributes) -> build_matsim_run_inputs (per scenario x day: day-filtered mapped schedule, fleet capacities via transit_fleet, regex-patched run network, parking prices, config emitted through registry.param_config). build_manifest walks the city tree and resolves lineage from each script's OUTPUT_INPUTS declaration. Mumbai carries its own parallel pipeline under cities/mumbai/build/ (build_baseline_run_inputs.py re-implements assembly for the bound_fields scoring path). Since 16 September 2026 the three largest builders were "staged" by src/setup/extract_loop_body.py into 32 functions whose only parameter is a types.SimpleNamespace carrying 2-29 names of the former enclosing scope.

risksrc/build/build_population.py373Two modelling values are typed inline and pass the hardcoding gate: household size capped at 10 (line 373) and the top age drawn up to 95 (line 400); check_hardcoding exempts every literal that is a direct argument of min()/max().B.population.household_size_top_band_mean is declared and swept, but the geometric tail it parameterises is truncated at 10 persons, so the realised 6+ band mean sits below the declared one whatever the sweep says; the report records top_band_mean_drawn but no check compares it.new
risksrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py653Motorbike (and resident truck) persons are carved by a hash against the target identity and locked to the mode (lockedMode at line 1164), so the motorbike share is delivered by construction, not by choice.Motorbike reads -7.3 % (ok) at F36 it.230, but that level is the carve solving to CAL.mode_split, so it cannot evidence choice accuracy; a policy that changes motorbike cost moves nothing.still open

architecture
run.py is the front door: it resolves the registry through overlays, runs the issue gate and preflight, and on Windows detaches itself under the Task Scheduler (a .cmd wrapper carrying CITYSIM_LAUNCH_STAMP and the city). The child calls run_matsim.run(): reconcile stale cards, find_completed (identity = parameters + controler/values/inputs sha256), subsample plans and scale transit capacity (sample_population), emit config through the builder's emitter, write _meta.json, launch the JVM, and start three daemon watchers (gate via report_mode_ridership subprocess, wall ceiling, stall) that write a marker then kill. Terminal paths close out through close_out() (record, summary, processed mirror, trim). results_store owns raw/processed and trimming; procs owns liveness (card_pid_alive, boot-time aware since this commit).

architecture
One reader decides every mode reading: report_mode_ridership.report() (board, gate watcher, objective, store snapshots all call it), which reads an iteration's trips/legs through iteration_reading (decoded once per process, 6-table LRU) or derives trips from experienced plans (iteration_trips), resolves residents from the run's own _residents.csv.gz (extract_metrics.home_lga), and scores against mode_targets_by_mode.csv. extract_metrics writes _metrics.json (at the newest table at or below reached_iteration for a stopped arm); fit.py scores the calibration split only and adds goal_modes from the same reader; calibrate.py wraps run_matsim/extract/fit into a coordinate-descent search or a constrained base (C5). build_status_board renders the board from the same reader, clamped to reached_iteration.

architecture
src/registry/__init__.py is the resolver: registry JSON per city -> scenario/day/run overlays -> env -> --set, each layer checked for membership, sweep (every numeric leaf, #200), categorical membership and held_fixed; unobtained fields raise on get(). param_config emits the MATSim config from matsim_param bindings and closure() refuses a leak; outputs.write_checked validates run/meta/metrics/fit documents against config/schema/outputs. The checks are scripts under tests/ and src/registry/ run by session_gate and CI: manifest integrity, hardcoding ledger (9 categories, at 0), document currency/shape/links, city agnosticism, the import sweep and 578 unit tests in 106 files.

testability
The resolver and output contracts are exercised by many tests (test_leaf_sweeps, test_outputs, test_param_config, test_override_reaches_the_run). Of the 11 src/registry modules only 3 are imported by a unit test: check_city, check_legacy_drift, check_matsim_defaults, render_docs, render_schema, sweep_ledger and extract_legacy_constants run only as CI scripts, so a vacuous pass in them is found by nobody. The checks have no tests of their own blind spots (the min/max exemption would have been caught by one).

architecture
Per-city extract scripts. Newcastle: fetchers (fetch_gtfs, fetch_open_data, fetch_abs_dem, fetch_tpa_daily, overpass with extents derived from the LGA boundary and the corridor stop set) that land raw bytes under data/raw with provenance_*.json, plus readers (reader_shapes) that adapt survey/census tables to the framework's declared shapes. Mumbai: a catalogue-driven acquirer (acquire_sources, harvest packs with an allowlist and redirect-host refusal) and ~100 evidence builders (harbour line, census geographies, controls). build_manifest turns both into MANIFEST.csv with stage, lineage scope, licence and share-alike verdicts.

defectcities/mumbai/data/MANIFEST.csv1579 of Mumbai's raw manifest rows carry no retrieval date (210 transit, 71 population, 59 boundaries, ...), and 9 processed rows have lineage_scope none with no producing script.A reader asking when data/raw/transit/... was retrieved, or which script made data/processed/derived/vehicle_possession_growth.csv, gets a blank; the reproducibility gate ("regenerable by a committed script ... retrieval date") is unmet for those rows while CI is green.new
risksrc/build/build_activity_chains.py2,654The calibration-split AADT stations seed the through and freight tiers' volumes and are then scored by fit.py counts, so the same observations enter demand and fit.Counts error improves because demand was drawn from those counts, not because routing or choice is right; the holdout is untouched, but the calibration counts statistic is partly circular.new
riskcities/newcastle/data/MANIFEST.csv133 processed Newcastle rows have no source or retrieval date (C1 parameter tables, the per-day vehicles.xml files), because their producers declare no raw ancestor.params/C1_parameters.json - the scoring table - reads as source-less in the published manifest.new
smellcities/mumbai/extract/build_harbour_mapped_routes.py50The harbour-line evidence builders are single mains of complexity 78-82 (build_harbour_mapped_routes, build_harbour_service_evidence, build_harbour_path_candidates, build_harbour_track_evidence).A change to one geometric rule cannot be tested without running the whole script on the raw PDFs.new

testability
The extract layer is deliberately outside the import sweep (it downloads at import). Unit tests exist for the host allowlist (test_provenance_hosts_allowed), the API-key handling (test_acquisition_api_key), MMR extent names, the regional bus feed offsets and the GTFS cache; the Newcastle fetchers and reader_shapes (the survey adapter every target and seed reads through) and nearly all Mumbai evidence builders have none.

architecture
citysim.CitysimControler assembles the MATSim Controler (one 607-line assemble()) and binds ~30 extensions by config group: availability and gated subtour mode choice, the ride pairing engine (BeforeMobsim pairing, JointRideEngine physical boarding, AfterMobsim restore through RemodeRestore), the taxi fleet (BeforeMobsim greedy allocation), the household vehicle roster, scoring add-ons (crowding, service quality, bike stress, parking, fares), routers (gradient link speed, raptor mode cost, direct walk) and RunTelemetry. Handlers keep HashMaps written on event threads and read at BeforeMobsim, relying on the sim-step barrier that RunTelemetry.requireSimStepBarrier and the launcher refusal enforce. src/java_signals/ carries the signals contrib entry point, SCATS and tram priority controllers on a separate Maven stack.

1defectbuild layersrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py:1246The external boundary tier is missing from the F36 plans (the first rebuild, 22 September, after the 16 September refactor): the staging refactor (5b8f54f6) moved the B1 lookup ahead of the tier test for every tier but through/freight, so each external agent returns unwritten. Counted: the chains hold 6,103 external agents (12,206 weekday trips); population_WEEKDAY.xml.gz holds 0 (616,040 = 510,383 person + 89,393 freight + 16,264 through).F36 arm 0 simulated the region without its boundary commuters (the F35 plans predate the refactor): their road volumes on the entry corridors and any rail boardings they make are absent, and no check compares plans persons with the chains report by tier. The refactor was declared byte-identical and never executed on this tier.
2defectcontract and checkscities/newcastle/registry/RUN_execution.json:595RUN.transit_router.access_max_radius_m is misderived: its identity says 1,000 + 200 m is "the furthest the beeline path could ever reach", but the beeline stop finder falls back to the NEAREST stop wherever it is (the #162 measurement proved exactly that fallback). With network access (§9.167) the 1,200 m cap turns every trip end beyond it into no transit route at all.Measured on this pass: every 25 % run before 12 September counted 31-37 % of pt requests with no transit route; every run since, 66-68 % (F36 arm 0: 1,789,120 of 2,699,995). Re-routed offline on F36's own plans without the cap, the same trips give 38.8-39.4 %. About 27 points of "no route" - and a 9 km mean walk handed to a pt chooser - are this value. Three F35 results and F36 carry it.
3defectMATSim extensionssrc/java/citysim/TaxiFleetEngine.java:243A served taxi request's wait is computed and averaged for the log (meanWait 963-977 s on F36 arm 0) and never executed or scored: the agent departs at once and pays only the 5-minute wait folded into the constant.Taxi is 16 minutes more attractive than the fleet it rides on can deliver, and refuses 29 % of requests, which are then walked; taxi reads +107.3 % (F36 it.230) and +133.3 % (F35 result). Repeat of the previous report's finding.
4defectanalysis and calibrationsrc/analyse/arm_cost.py:193setup_seconds takes wall minus the iteration sum, so a run whose host died books the dead time as setup.After the reboot the pricer quotes the next 25 % arm at 62.9 h (37.8 h of "setup"); from the run's own clock it is ~25.6 h (setup 1,598 s). A stated-cost approval would be asked on a figure 2.5x too high.

Now read at 230, and procs.card_pid_alive treats every card pid as dead once the host booted after started.
6defectrun harnesssrc/run/run_matsim.py:148A raw --set override for a plain MATSim parameter is applied with re.sub and no match check (setp), so a name that is absent from the emitted config is silently ignored while the run record lists it in overrides as applied; set_mode_param (line 153) refuses the same case for modeParams.run.py --set brainExpBeta=2 (or any typo, or a param living in a module the config does not emit) produces a run whose _run.json says overrides {brainExpBeta: 2} and whose config.xml still carries the registry value - the record states a change the run never executed (the "override must reach the run" defect class, raw channel). refuse_unrealised_overrides (line 838) tests registry keys only.

12riskrun harnesssrc/run/run_matsim.py:765Nothing prevents or survives a host reboot: no launch check reads a pending restart or an update pause; a closed-out arm cannot be warm-started; a post-cutoff checkpoint is refused by the innovation-fraction sweep.Windows Update restarted the host at 04:30 on 24 September, 30 minutes after its active hours closed, killing F36 arm 0 at iteration 237 of 250 (~50 minutes from its record). the_gap_243_vs_469_5
  • 1. Probe vs arm at the same iterations (-16 %): the probe's it.2-3 ran 482/457 s (replanning 134/134, beforeMobsim 71/71, mobsim 269/246); the arm's own it.2-5 ran 391-404 s (replanning 103-107, beforeMobsim 61-62, mobsim 217-223). Every phase is ~20 % lower on one build and one demand, so the difference is the host's condition at 02:24-03:40 while the probe ran, NOT the model; nothing records host load, so it cannot be attributed further.
  • 2. The early-iteration fall (392 -> ~345 s by it.50-99): beforeMobsimListeners 60 -> 20 s because the seed's taxi demand collapses. At it.0 TaxiFleetEngine had 56,782 requests against fleet 200 (declared 800 x 0.25), refused 45,833 (80.7 %) and routed them as network walks in 54.5 s; by it.230 13,218 requests, 3,893 refused, 3.5 s (matsim.log head and tail). Replanning drifts 105 -> 88-92 s. The same shape is on every F35/F36 pair: probe it.2-3 425-470 s against arm recurring 348-360 s (performance.json).
  • 3. Two contention episodes, unattributed: it.100-130 (14:30-18:00 on 23 Sep) and it.174-199 (22:30-01:30) ran 400-436 s with every phase up 20-30 % at once (replanning 106-138, mobsim 246-277), against 316-345 s either side. About 3,200 s + ~1,000 s of excess.
  • 4. The innovation-off tail (it.200-237, cutoff 0.8 x 250): replanning falls from ~93 s to 1-2 s and beforeMobsim to 14-19 s; mobsim stays 208-226 s, so a tail iteration is 234-264 s (median of non-dump tail iterations 256.5 s; last ten 234-264 s).
  • So 469.5 s was never the recurring cost: it is an early, contended, innovating iteration. The arm's own plain median is 349.5 s over 226 iterations (arm_cost.py), 360 s innovating (it.2-199 non-dump) and 256.5 s in the tail.

our_listeners
beforeMobsimListeners
RidePairingEngine.notifyBeforeMobsim (src/java/citysim/RidePairingEngine.java:497) walks every selected plan in id order, indexes drivers by household, pairs ride legs and routes declared-pair detours on global.numberOfThreads workers; ride_pairing.csv elapsed_ms median 9,042 (it.2-49) -> 13,792 (it.200-237). It allocates a fresh HashMap current and per-iteration DriverLeg/RideLeg lists for every car and ride leg (~363 k car departures). TaxiFleetEngine.notifyBeforeMobsim (TaxiFleetEngine.java:200) collects every taxi request, runs a fleet queue and re-modes refusals as network walks: 52-56 s an iteration at it.0-6, 3-4 s at it.230-237. The rest of the phase is MATSim's own dump all plans (nested, 198-229 s on the 11 dump iterations).
hoistable
The pairing's household index, licence map and person ordering (ordered, household, licensed) are per-run facts and are already fields; what is per-iteration is genuinely the selected plans. The taxi refusal routing is per-iteration by design. Nothing large is hoistable on this reading; the ~40 s of early-iteration taxi walking is a seed-demand cost, not a code one.

scaling_with_fraction
The sampling page states no pace-vs-fraction law. performance.json: 1 % at 8 threads 30.25 s median, 25 % at 16 threads 347.34 s median - but these span families (pre-footpath 1 % vs post-footpath 25 %) and so cannot be read as a scaling curve; no same-family 1 %/10 %/25 % triple exists. unmeasured - needs a probe arm (one family, three fractions, 4 iterations each).
headroom
The mobsim is 15.5 h of the arm's 24.2 h of iterations and has no measured config lever (threads flat, oneThreadPerHandler fatal, synchronizeOnSimSteps=false a regression, FIFO refused on correctness - 9.59). Its split between walk movement, signals and event handling is unmeasured - needs a probe arm (the JFR thread-state probe of recommendation 20260916T062246:9, still open).

warm start

what_happened
Windows Update (TrustedInstaller, System event 1074) rebooted the host at 04:30 on 24 September during iteration 238 of 250, ~50 min before the arm would have finished; the harness and JVM died with the host; the dead arm sat until run.py --stop closed it out at 17:43 on 25 September as stopped_by_operator.
host_state_read_today
HKLM ... WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\RebootRequired absent; Component Based Servicing\RebootPending absent; WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings ActiveHoursStart 11, ActiveHoursEnd 4 (11:00-04:00, 17 h); PauseUpdatesExpiryTime not set; no WindowsUpdate\AU policy key. The reboot came 30 minutes after active hours ended.
prevent_today
Nothing. No launch check reads a pending reboot, active hours or an update pause (grep of src/ for RebootPending / ActiveHours / WindowsUpdate: no hits). procs.card_pid_alive / boot_time (this commit) only recognise a reboot AFTER the fact so --stop does not kill a recycled pid.
prevent_options
optioneffortlimit
preflight refusal: read RebootRequired, RebootPending and PendingFileRenameOperations; refuse a launch while a reboot is pending~0.5 day with a winreg-mocked unit testcatches a reboot already staged, not one staged mid-arm (the TrustedInstaller servicing that killed F36 may have staged after launch)
active hoursnone in codeWindows caps active hours at 18 h; a ~25.6 h arm always crosses the out-of-hours window (here 04:00-11:00) at least once, so active hours alone cannot protect an arm
require an update pause covering the ceiling: preflight reads PauseUpdatesExpiryTime and refuses (or warns) when it ends before launch + RUN.gate.wall_ceiling_h; the operator pauses in Settings (Home allows 1-5 weeks)~0.5 daythe operator's action, not the harness's; the cheapest real protection
NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers policy valuean admin registry change by the operatorwhether Windows 11 Home honours it is unverified here
survive_today
Only by hand: run.py --warm-start <dead_run_dir> (#75, 9.76) starts a new run from the newest output/ITERS/it.N/N.plans.xml.gz with firstIteration = N; output_plans.xml.gz is deliberately not used (written only at a clean shutdown). RULED a result: a warm-completed arm keeps ran_to_last_iteration with warm_started_from as provenance (9.167, #192, superseding 9.76's open question), because no two runs of one build are bit-identical anyway (9.142).
why_F36_arm0_cannot_be_warm_started_as_built
  • resolve_warm_start (src/run/run_matsim.py:165) refuses any run whose _run.json exists: arm 0 was closed out as stopped_by_operator, so it is refused as 'stopped deliberately'. A host death is a crash, but the only close-out path labels it an operator stop.
  • warm_start_overrides (run_matsim.py:975) keeps the cutoff iteration by setting f' = (cutoff - N)/(last - N) through the registry, whose sweep for RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation is [0.7, 0.9] (cities/newcastle/registry/RUN_execution.json:274). On 250 x 0.8 only N <= 83 passes; the newest checkpoint it.225 gives f' = -1.0 and is refused. A resume after the cutoff - the cheapest case, since nothing innovates - has no path.
build_costs
changeeffort
close a host-reboot death as a crash (a distinct completion such as host_rebooted, read from procs.boot_time > card started) that warm start accepts~0.5 day
post-cutoff resume: when N >= cutoff, start with innovation disabled from firstIteration instead of deriving a negative fraction; pre-cutoff, bypass the sweep for the derived value with the parent's cutoff recorded~0.5-1 day with unit tests
resume on boot: the detach wrapper already registers a scheduled task (run.py:472); add an /sc onstart (or onlogon) task per live arm that runs run.py --warm-start on its directory and re-arms the ceiling for the remaining quote, deleted at the arm's end~1 day; needs the two changes above
true in-iteration checkpointing (travel times, RNG state, our engines' state)weeks of Java against MATSim internals; not recommended
what_a_resume_would_have_cost
from it.225: ~0.44 h setup + 25 tail iterations at ~250 s + dumps at 225/250 ~ 2.3 h, against a fresh arm at ~25.6 h (arm_cost with the setup corrected)
comparability
Same controler, values and inputs hashes, so the resumed run stays inside F36 and is a result under 9.167. What resets: the RNG stream and MATSim's travel-time memory, and our engines' in-memory state - RidePairingEngine's previous map (the finished mobsim the pairing reads) is empty on the first resumed iteration, and TaxiFleetEngine's refusal set; score memory travels with the plans. After the cutoff no plan is created, so the reset reaches only selection and one iteration's pairing; whether that first iteration pairs fewer rides is unmeasured - needs a probe arm. Before the cutoff the reset also changes routes and mode innovation, so it reads as a band like any other replicate (9.142).

Verdict on the 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon is reachable at the measured pace: F36's arm 0 spent 24.17 h in 238 iterations (plain median 349.5 s; 360 s innovating, 256.5 s after the cutoff) plus 26.6 min of setup, and was ~50 minutes from finishing (about 25.5 h in all) when Windows Update rebooted the host. The 33.2 h quote came from a probe that ran every phase ~20 % slower than the arm's own same iterations and carried the seed's taxi refusals; the 62.9 h quote arm_cost.py gives today is a defect: it books the 37 h the dead host sat before close-out as setup. The corrected price for a fresh 25 % arm on this build is ~25.6 h (spread 24.7-34.0 h). What threatens the horizon now is not the pace but the host: nothing prevents or survives a reboot, and warm start refuses this arm twice. Halving the arm (~12.8 h) is not reachable by the measured, result-preserving levers: host quiet (1.0-1.3 h), plans interval (0.3-0.5 h), cached input routing (0.3-0.4 h) and GC (0-0.8 h, unmeasured) add up to 2-3 h. The rest must come from the two phases the footpath network grew: replanning (5.5 h; up to 3.8 h back if it returns to its pre-F34 25 s) and the mobsim (15.5 h, 81 % of whose departures are walk legs), whose split is unmeasured and needs one JFR probe each. Only a mobsim change - most plausibly walk off the qsim, which reverses the F34 decision and opens a family - or a shorter innovating horizon (both touch results) could halve it.

Since the previous pass

Against report #12 (16 September) and its reference run 20260916T063903_250it_25pct: plain recurring 348.5 -> 349.5 s (flat); record median 349.45 -> 354.04 s; replanning 89 -> 93 s; mobsim 245 -> 223 s; beforeMobsim 21 -> 23 s; dump all plans 191 -> 209 s and 6 -> 11 dumps (plans interval 50 -> 25); plans bytes 6.05 -> 9.69 GB; GC pause share 2.9 -> 3.5 %; peak used 42,933 -> 41,112 MB; departures per wall second 7,899.5 -> 7,714.9; stuck median 4,641 -> 6,266. New since: the first arm lost to a host reboot (at it.237), the pricer's dead-time setup defect (62.9 h quote), and warm start's two refusals of a post-cutoff, closed-out crash. Still open and repeated: the JFR mobsim probe (20260916T062246:9), build timing in the collector (20260914T152907:17, 20260916T062246:18), and the nested-phase ratio above 1 in the tail (share_of_parent_when_it_runs 11.421 on this arm).

verdict
Prefix, sections, disclaimers and no-attribution are held almost without exception; title length is the one convention broken by habit (60 of 90 over 72 characters, worsening after 1 Sep). Honesty is the strongest trait: 11 conclusions were corrected in the open by a later PR, and no PR claims a result it did not have.

what the comparison says

  • Nobody in 58 projects validates every simulated mode on its own ridership: the top rung is empty in the field, and this project is still the only attempt (2 of 12 inside 10 % on F36 arm 0 at iteration 230, not a result).
  • Tap data is used as a validation source only per system, never per mode across a city: Cape Town MyCiTi (AFC boardings, R2 0.85), Seoul (T-money station boardings), Munich (stop-level MVV boardings). Riga uses taps as demand, not as a check.
  • Trip length is a calibration target in the field (Lausitz, Berlin, Leipzig, mobiTopp, POLARIS, Rotterdam, now Jakarta) but no one publishes a tolerance; the levers are a per-mode marginal utility of distance, distance-group constants, or destination choice - never the mode constant alone.
  • The motorcycle is a calibrated majority mode only in Greater Jakarta (10 %, about 3 million agents, priced by distance); this project's motorbike is one of its two modes inside 10 %.
  • Bike destination choice as its own constrained sub-module (Okanagan 2026) is the field's answer to an over-chosen, over-long bike; this project has a bike distance cost but no bike-specific destination set.
  • The agencies recalibrate mode choice after release as routine (MWCOG Ver. 1.1.0, February and April 2026 memos), and still disagree with their own trip-based models on transit ridership.
  • Run cost: the only published 25 % MATSim wall time on a current release is Kelheim v3.0 (~15.5 h, ~139 s a recurring iteration, ~120,000 residents); no one publishes a 25 % heap. MWCOG's ActivitySim needs 206 GB RAM; BEAM 512 GB for 12 h at 30 %.
  • The on-demand modes scale with the sample: BEAM finds ride-hail share and efficiency rise steeply from 10 % to 40 % and flatten after - taxi at 25 % sits on the steep part.

A1AResidential location (fixed from census)INsrc/build/build_activity_chains.py:329 (B.population.home_jitter_radius_factor; home from the census SA1)nothing on the board; residence is fixed by designResidential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the built-environment effect and mis-states only the self-selected minority.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S02642751210018522026-09-07
A2AWorkplace locationPARTIALsrc/build/build_zone_attractions.py:8 (workplace-weighted POI index within SA2); no JTW OD read by the chains buildercar/pt trip length (pt 12.96 vs 23.4 km) via where commutes goWorkplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2112.120712026-09-08
A3AVehicle ownership per householdINsrc/java/citysim/CitysimControler.java:495-501 HouseholdVehicleRoster (B.population.vehicle_roster = census)car +4.0 % is inside the band; the roster makes the car-less quarter whose alternatives failHousehold car ownership is one of the strongest single predictors of mode: an increase in car ownership raises the probability of commuting by car and depresses active and transit modes, with a reported elasticity of -2.643 for the substitution of active modes. Income, household size, distance to centre, accessibility to shops/services/employment and intersection density are the dominant explanatory variables.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S13619209240004402026-09-07
A4AVehicle type (EV, e-bike)OUTno e-bike or EV attribute in src/java/citysim or the population builders (grep: none)bike trip length (8.32 vs 5.20 km) only if an e-bike class were added; lowThe e-bike evidence is now meta-analysed: across experimental studies, access to an e-bike adds about 5 km of daily travel and raises e-bike mode share by about 26 percentage points, while car use falls by about 2.4 km a day (a 10% drop in car mode share); single controlled trials report car share falling 21%, and older meta-studies put e-bike-for-car substitution at 43% of trips and 63% of mileage. The effect is context-dependent: where cycling is already high the e-bike substitutes conventional cycling; where it is low it draws from car and public transport. (Figures are abstract-level; the full text was not retrievable this pass.)https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01441647.2025.24745562026-09-07
A5ALicence holdingINsrc/build/build_population.py:95 (B.population.licence_rate_by_age_band, measured)ride/car split via who can driveLicence holding among people under 35 has fallen across Australia, the UK, the US, Canada and much of Europe: TfNSW reports 65.4% of 16-20 year olds licensed in 2017, 8.3 points below 2001 and 8.1 below 2009, with the proportion licensed at age 30 also declining cohort on cohort. The travel-behaviour consequence named is a greater reliance on getting a lift, especially in wealthy suburbs and high-car-ownership families, and more public transport, walking and cycling in less wealthy areas.https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/system/files/media/documents/2017/Why%20are%20young%20people%20driving%20less%20-%20Trends%20in%20licence-holding%20and%20travel%20behaviour_0.pdf2026-09-07
A6APublic-transport passes / concessionsPARTIALsrc/java/citysim/PtFareChargeHandler.java:62 child/senior tables and daily caps (A.fare.*); no period passespt level marginallyA smartcard natural experiment on Dutch fares separates pass holders from single-ticket users: passengers on a monthly or annual subscription have the highest travel frequency per origin-destination pair per week - almost twice that of single-ticket users - and the estimated fare elasticities split cleanly between the frequent-user products (pay-as-you-go, student and subscription) and the occasional ones (end-of-month and single tickets). A pass converts the fare from a per-trip price to a zero marginal cost, and the behavioural response is the frequency, not the mode.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0967070X2100055X2026-09-07

B5BDay-type differences (weekday, Saturday, Sunday)PARTIALsrc/build/build_activity_chains.py:169 (B.activity.day_purpose_mix per day type); B.activity.weekend_to_weekday is DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS CONSUMER (check_hardcoding.py section 1)nothing on the weekday boardWeekend travel has a different shape, not just a different volume: the sharp early-morning and mid-afternoon weekday peaks are absent on the weekend day because so few trips are to and from work, and social-recreational and personal-business travel spread more evenly across the day become the dominant influence; weekend travel raises car-pooling for both youth and adults but has no measured effect on transit use, and destination land use shifts toward residential.https://nhts.ornl.gov/2009/pub/Weekday%20Travel%20FAQ.pdf2026-09-07

E7EPerson attributes: age and sexPARTIALsrc/java/citysim/ModeAvailabilityConfigGroup.java:28 (age gates: B.taxi.min_unaccompanied_age 18, B.population.bike_min_age 12) and fare age bands; no sex termbike (12-17 year olds over-represented on earlier arms)Age and sex segment travel with a transferable magnitude on the ACTIVE modes. Across 19 major cities in 13 countries and 6 continents (8 low-and-middle-income, 11 high-income), females are more likely than males to walk in every city - on average 23% more likely - and on average 6% more likely to use public transport, while the relation REVERSES for cycling, where women are typically about half as likely to cycle as men; in high-cycling cities the two genders are equally likely, and in Berlin, Munich and Hamburg women cycle more than men. The gap is age-dependent: among children under 16 the metrics are often equal, and the disparity widens with age. On age itself, older travellers drive, walk and take taxis and make little use of bicycles or rideshare, car use falls and dependence on transit rises as the ability to drive falls, and older women are the group most likely to use public transport; an urban Italian study puts men at ~1.5x the odds of choosing a private car over an active mode. No Australian mode-choice model published an age or sex coefficient this pass could read.https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614415/2026-09-07

F1FRoute choice and re-routingINresults/raw/20260923T034632_250it_25pct/config.xml:193 ReRoute strategy (RUN.replanning.weights ReRoute 0.15)noneRoute choice is estimated on GPS-observed routes with path-size logit corrections for overlapping paths, and the observed share taking the shortest path is small: over 25,157 trips by 143 subjects tracked for 8-13 weeks in Minneapolis-St Paul, 34% of all trips exactly matched the shortest-travel-time path and 40% matched within a 10% tolerance, while for commute trips alone the figures were 13.5% and 21.7%; no subject followed a shortest-DISTANCE path unless it coincided with the shortest-time one. About 50% of trips were within 30 s and about 90% within 5 minutes of the shortest-time route, so the deviation is wide in route space and narrow in time. H1HUtility form (Charypar-Nagel scoring)INsrc/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1410 (C.scoring.performing_utils_per_h 6.0; Charypar-Nagel)allMATSim's scoring is the Charypar-Nagel form: plan utility is the sum of activity utilities plus travel disutilities, with activity utility beta_dur * t_typ * ln(t_dur / t_0) - marginal utility of duration against a typical duration and a minimal duration below which utility is negative - and leg score built from a mode constant, a marginal disutility of travel duration, and a marginal disutility of distance. Under iteration the population's average plan score stabilises at a point where individuals cannot unilaterally improve.https://www.matsim.org/doxygen/classorg_1_1matsim_1_1core_1_1scoring_1_1functions_1_1_charypar_nagel_scoring_function_factory.html2026-09-07

H3HChoice-set generation and mode availabilityINsrc/java/citysim/AvailabilityModesCalculator.java:59 and GatedSubtourModeChoice; coverage at it.229: ride 19.09 %, pt 14.34 %, taxi 45.36 %, bike 21.90 %, walk 52.09 % (output/modeChoiceCoverage1x.txt)ride -13.7 % (coverage bound)The choice set in an agent-based model is generated, not enumerated: MATSim's SubtourModeChoice changes the mode of all legs of one randomly chosen subtour to a randomly chosen alternative, and offers a mode only where the choice would not require a resource to appear out of thin air - chain-based modes assume one resource per mode, initially at home. H4HLearning, replanning, plan memory, innovation switch-offINsrc/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1323 (RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation 0.8)allThe distinction that governs convergence: while innovation is switched on - new routes, new times - the result is NOT truly stationary; if innovation is switched off the process is stationary but limited to the plans each agent holds at that moment. The plan set is the agent's choice set, and MATSim's recommended control is fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation rather than a per-strategy disable iteration. ADDED 8 September 2026: what the loop is converging TO is stated by MATSim's own equilibrium work - an approximate minimisation of an equilibrium gap that measures, per agent, how much it could improve by changing its plan while all others keep theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium'. Reproducible computation of a point equilibrium is named as the single most important advantage of the four-step model that MATSim does not have by default. See the new factor 'Equilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?'.https://matsim.org/docs/userguide/terminology.html2026-09-08
H5HLLM-driven agentsOUTnone (grep)noneTwo 2025-2026 results now bracket this lane. On the optimistic side, GATSim integrates LLM-powered generative agents - hierarchical memory, multi-modal retrieval, planning, reactive and reflection processes, diverse socioeconomic profiles and lifelong learning - into an urban mobility environment, and reports validation at microscopic and macroscopic levels, claiming agents 'perform competitively with human annotators in role-playing scenarios' while 'naturally producing realistic macroscopic traffic patterns'; its abstract states no accuracy figure, no real city and no cost per agent-day. On the sceptical side, the first systematic evaluation against observed mobility (2026) measures AgentSociety and CitySim over Greater Paris (3,337 residents, 7 days) and Shanghai (58,502 users, 10 days) and separates 'face validity' from 'objective mobility realism': AgentSociety's travel-distance error is a Wasserstein distance of 14.83 plus or minus 0.35 km and CitySim's 7.53 plus or minus 1.67 km, with origin-destination similarity at a common-part-of-commuters of 0.138 plus or minus 0.018; trip-duration error is 24.41 plus or minus 0.24 minutes and dwell-time error 3.96 plus or minus 0.12 hours, against reference-sample variability of 0.29 minutes and 0.26 hours. Activity PROPORTIONS come out well (Jensen-Shannon divergence 0.0296) while activity SEQUENCES do not (0.1125), and mobility diversity is 'unstable across default prompting configurations'. The finding to carry: LLM agents reproduce qualitative mobility laws and aggregate activity mixes, and miss individual spatial behaviour by one to two orders of magnitude more than sampling error.https://arxiv.org/html/2606.138352026-09-08
H6HEquilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?PARTIALsrc/analyse/progress_digest.py:10 (RUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp 0.5 reported, not a stop rule)reading stabilityMATSim's mobsim/scoring/replanning loop is a Monte-Carlo co-evolutionary search, not a solved fixed point, and its own authors say so. Floetteroed's statement of the position is the clearest available: the assignment relies on approximate minimisation of an EQUILIBRIUM GAP measuring, for every agent, how much that agent could improve its score by changing its plan if all other agents kept theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium', and the method 'aims to reduce the gap in subsequent MATSim iterations, steering the simulation process towards a state that has a low gap, and hence may be deemed to be near an equilibrium point'. He names the reproducible computation of point equilibria as 'the single most important advantage' of the traditional four-step / static-assignment model - an advantage MATSim does not have by default - and supplies the emulation and greedo contribs that add gap minimisation to the loop, illustrated on a multimodal Greater Stockholm scenario with all-day route, departure-time and mode choice. The wider theory agrees: MATSim targets a STOCHASTIC user equilibrium (minimum PERCEIVED cost) rather than a Nash equilibrium; best-response dynamics carry no convergence guarantee, though if they converge they converge to an equilibrium. No published convergence rate exists for a multimodal MATSim scenario: relaxation is asserted by observation, not proved.https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/baug/ivt/ivt-dam/events/2023/09/05/abstracts/Floetteroed_MUM_2023.pdf2026-09-08
H7HIn-loop parameter estimation from a ground-truth subpopulationOUTno in-loop estimation in src/calibrate (grep)noneAn architecture that avoids the outer loop entirely: estimate the utility parameters INSIDE the simulation, against a subpopulation of real survey respondents whose observed plans are pinned. The MATSim planParamCalibration extension does exactly that - a designated subpopulation carries its surveyed plan under the KeepLastSelected strategy so those plans are the ground truth, the remaining agents generate alternatives by the ordinary strategies, and CMA-ES maximises a logit-like log-likelihood over the planCalcScore parameters (mode constants, marginal utility of travelling, of distance and of money, daily monetary constants, typical and minimal activity durations, line-switch, waiting, late-arrival and early-departure terms) at each MATSim iteration, writing the result back into the config for the next one. It stops on a designated iteration or on convergence, the default being an average estimated difference below 0.001. Tested on a 2023 street-interview trip-diary survey plus mobile-location commuting arrays at 100 m grid accuracy, the maximum log-likelihood is stable over twenty MATSim iterations and essentially unchanged whether the calibration population is respondents alone or respondents plus 100k, 300k, 600k or one million commuting records - the claimed proof that the estimator is auto-adaptive to population scale. The price of the architecture is exactly the data an aggregate-only city lacks: the likelihood's observations are unit-record plans.https://www.matsim.org/conferences/mum2024/presentations/MUM2024_Lu.pdf2026-09-08
H8HMachine-learned choice models in place of a hand-specified utilityOUTno learned choice model in src (grep); NSW HTS is aggregate-onlynone nowNeural choice models beat multinomial logit on prediction and lose on the quantity a twin is actually scored on. A utility-informed neural network trained on 14,671 trips from the 2017 US National Household Travel Survey for California reached 89.03% mode-choice accuracy, the highest in its benchmark against MNL and other classifiers; alternative-specific-utility deep networks (ASU-DNN) and residual-logit hybrids (ResLogit) are likewise consistently more accurate than MNL on the same data. The published caution is sharper than the accuracy claim: the models with the best DISAGGREGATE predictive performance - gradient-boosted trees and random forests - give POORER estimates of behavioural indicators and of AGGREGATE MODE SHARES than deep neural networks and than plain multinomial logit. Every method in this family is estimated on unit-record choice observations with the alternatives' attributes attached; none can be fitted to a published aggregate share table, and none has been shown to sit inside an equilibrium loop where the attributes of the alternatives are themselves simulation outputs.https://arxiv.org/html/1909.074812026-09-08

What the guidance does not describe is enforcement - no surveyed practice makes the holdout unreadable by construction.https://tfresource.org/topics/Model_calibration_and_validation2026-09-07

Empirically, between-seed variation in link loads dominates the variation between the last two iterations within one seed, so a within-run stability test alone is not evidence of convergence.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187705091830440X2026-09-07

I5ISensitivity sweepsPARTIALsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:15 (every assumed field carries a sweep); sweeps not executedallThe recommended method for agent-based models is variance-based global sensitivity analysis: because ABMs are non-linear, Sobol' indices decompose the output variance into first-order and total contributions of each parameter and its interactions, sampled with Sobol' sequences over the input space; one-at-a-time sweeps are the local, linear special case and miss interactions.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S09518320130009992026-09-07
I6IASC calibration methodINsrc/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py:19 (log-ratio, CAL.asc.damping 0.6)bike, walk constants (walk frozen by decision)The practice standard is an iterative adjustment rather than an estimation: compare the modelled split to the observed split, add the log ratio of observed to modelled share to each mode constant, re-run, and repeat until the split is inside a stated error threshold, commonly plus or minus one percentage point; ActivitySim applies the same increment to tour-level and trip-level constants together because tour mode conditions trip mode. The profession's own validation guidance is explicit that this is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted - 'the constants can easily be revised so that modeled mode shares match targets', which is precisely the danger, since a constant absorbs every omitted variable and every supply error along with the genuine preference. In an agent-based model the problem is harder than in a four-step model because the attributes of the alternatives are outcomes of the simulation, so the constants cannot be estimated by ordinary maximum likelihood at all; the MATSim-native answer (Rakow and Nagel 2024) is a simulation-based calibration that fine-tunes the ASCs to align simulated mode shares with reference data, and eqasim does the same through boptx.https://tfresource.org/topics/Model_Validation_and_Reasonableness_Checking_Mode_Choice.html2026-09-08
I7IAutomatic calibration: the search algorithm and its evaluation budgetPARTIALsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:710 (CAL.search.points_per_parameter 3, max_rounds 3); planned, not executed on a resultallCalibrating a microsimulation is a black-box, stochastic, expensive simulation-based optimisation problem, and the published methods separate by how many simulation evaluations they can afford. SPSA (simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation) is the field's workhorse because it costs only two simulation evaluations per gradient estimate whatever the dimension, and W-SPSA extends it with a weight matrix; but it is built for asymptotic guarantees rather than early termination, and under a small budget it barely moves - on a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions SPSA took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 117% over fifteen simulation iterations, while a metamodel method reached 32%. Evolutionary strategies (CMA-ES, xNES) and finite-difference gradient approximation (FDSA, SPSA) are what the MATSim/eqasim calibration framework boptx implements. The cross-entropy method is a Monte-Carlo importance-sampling search and is the most expensive family: one published SUMO calibration of a three-intersection model spent 98,304 simulation evaluations. Bayesian optimisation over a surrogate is the current answer for a small budget (see the surrogate row). The field states its own constraint plainly: computational budgets in the literature are 'one to two orders of magnitude lower than the problem dimension', and general-purpose algorithms 'are designed for asymptotic performance guarantees and are not designed to be terminated with such few function evaluations'.https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.113922026-09-08
I8ISurrogate / metamodel-assisted calibrationOUTnone in src/calibrate (grep)noneThe canonical line is Osorio's metamodel simulation-based optimisation: replace the expensive simulated objective with an analytical network model plus a low-order statistical correction, then solve a sequence of cheap analytical problems, so that good points are found from the first iterations without a large initial sample. Its strongest published demonstration is a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions, where within ONE simulation iteration the linear-metamodel method took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 32%, against 48% for a tailored linear-assignment method and 117% for SPSA, all inside a fifteen-simulation-iteration budget - and 'thereafter there is not much improvement within such few iterations', i.e. nearly all the gain arrives at the first evaluation. The second family is machine-learned rather than analytical: a random-forest surrogate driving Bayesian optimisation calibrated 477 behavioural parameters of the SimMobility MT activity-based model for Tallinn, and did so against AGGREGATE benchmarks ('the modal share of the whole population'), reaching 4% error on the total number of trips and an average origin-destination error of 15.92 vehicles per day. That paper states no prior work had calibrated as many as 477 parameters and that existing rigorous methods 'do not consider more than a few dozen of parameters (the maximum number being 98)'.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.034802026-09-08
I9IIdentifiability under many simultaneous targetsPARTIALsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:484 (CAL.objective.independent_targets 10, derived); 5 of 67 targets scorableallA parameter set is identified only if distinct parameter values produce distinguishable outputs on the targets you actually hold, and the simulation-calibration literature is explicit that when a model is over-parametrised relative to its targets, 'non-identifiability can arise, making it theoretically impossible to locate the true parameter value'. The published remedy is not a better optimiser but a different answer: report an ELIGIBILITY SET - the set of all parameter values whose simulated outputs match the data - constructed to carry rigorous frequentist guarantees, extended to multivariate outputs by a feature-extraction-then-aggregation construction. The counting rule underneath is what binds a mode-share calibration: K shares that sum to one contain K-1 independent numbers, so scoring twelve modelled modes against a five-mode survey does not supply twelve independent targets. The only way to buy identifiability for more parameters is to add targets of a DIFFERENT kind - link counts, boardings, trip-length and duration distributions - not more shares of the same total. The OD-calibration literature reaches the same place from the other side: 'the problem is underdetermined ... there are typically an infinite number of vectors x that can reproduce these counts', which is why a regularisation term toward a prior seed matrix is standard.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.128932026-09-08

The profession's own validation manual warns that revising constants is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted, because a constant absorbs every omitted variable. (2) BLP-STYLE DEMAND INVERSION: a contraction mapping inverts observed market shares to implied mean utilities and GMM on instrumented moments recovers heterogeneous taste coefficients 'from only aggregate market-share data', removing the IIA restriction on substitution; the requirement is instruments with genuine cross-market variation, which a single-city model does not naturally possess. (3) SURROGATE-ASSISTED SIMULATION-BASED ESTIMATION against aggregate benchmarks: the Tallinn SimMobility work fitted 477 behavioural parameters entirely against 'aggregate benchmarks (e.g., the modal share of the whole population)' and names disaggregate data only as future work - a direct feasibility proof that unit records are not a precondition for fitting a large behavioural parameter set.https://tfresource.org/topics/Model_Validation_and_Reasonableness_Checking_Mode_Choice.html2026-09-08
